text:
leo: quick checkpoint from the infra spike: we've got three candidate paths for supporting customer IP preservation without burning 1 ENI/tenant. want quick thumbs.

anya: TL;DR?

leo: 1) Full per-tenant private endpoint (isolation, static IPs). 2) Shared regional proxy + per-tenant NAT mappings (reserve a small pool of public/private IPs mapped to tenant id). 3) Shared proxy + sticky source port translation + session pinning (cheapest, hacky).

frank: Option 2 looks promising: keeps ENI count low, gives stable egress IPs for auth allowlists. But needs an idempotent NAT mapping service and a routing shim.

anya: Important: enterprise legal asks for audit trail and key pinning (mutual TLS). Option 2 supports that as long as the per-tenant mapping also provisions cert SANs and a tenant-specific mTLS identity.

devops-bot: note: loadtest job #789 queued (will run in 20m)

leo: ran a quick perf pass: with option 2, SNAT port usage dropped ~60% compared to naive regional NAT because we can route heavy flows to reserved IPs. tail latency delta ~+5-10ms for cold-starts due to extra hop.

frank: can you paste the sketch of the NAT mapping API?

leo: sure:
```
POST /nat-mappings
{ "tenant": "T123", "count": 2, "ttl": 86400 }
GET /nat-mappings/T123
DELETE /nat-mappings/T123
```
Mapping service allocates from a pool and writes a route for the tenant to the mapping device.

anya: what's the failure mode if mapping service loses state?

leo: we persist in dynamo + reconcile with periodic scans. if lost, tenant falls back to regional proxy (no preserved IP). rollback is simple: delete mapping + update route. but we need guardrails.

frank: ops concerns: how do we do peering updates? per-tenant route injection to customer VPC vs NAT mapping both need careful security rules. we should avoid per-tenant BGP where possible.

product-beth: customers asking for a non-transient egress IP solution this quarter. enterprise deals waiting. we need ETA and risk summary.

leo: proposal: ship option 2 as opt-in for Private plan customers. Default remains shared regional proxy for self-serve. rollout: alpha with 3 tenants -> beta with 20 -> GA. include feature flag + Console toggle + billing meter.

anya: control-plane contract needed: API to request mappings, status endpoints, a tenant lifecycle hook for delete/transfer, and an audit log accessible to SOC. Also permissions: who can create mapping? support + account-admin only.

frank: for automation: terraform module to create mapping + peering entries. we should codify the route flip sequence: 1) create mapping 2) allocate IPs 3) reconcile NAT device 4) update control-plane routing policy 5) wait health probes 6) flip DNS TTLs 7) deprecate regional path. Rollback reverses in order.

leo: test checklist I want: SNAT port saturation under multi-tenant load, failover when mapping service is down, cert reprovision latencies, billing accuracy, and security review for cross-tenant leakage.

devops-bot: loadtest #789 started. link: https://go/loadtest/789

anya: add a mandatory danger-zone checklist for ops to avoid accidentally assigning the same reserved IP twice. idempotency matters.

product-beth: pricing note: reserved egress IPs should be billable as an add-on. include charge per-IP-hour + a base mapping fee. I'll draft numbers with revenue ops.

frank: one more note: monitoring. We need per-mapping SNAT metrics, 95/99p latency to the mapping device, and a taggable alert to notify on port exhaustion.

leo: I'll write a short RFC follow-up doc capturing option 2 design + API + rollout plan. tagging you both for review. target: EOD Tue.

anya: I'll own cert/mTLS design and SOC audit shape.

product-beth: I'll sync pricing with finance and update the Console mockups.

leo: ok team. reconvene Thurs 11am PT to review test output and decide GA window.

devops-bot: loadtest #789 completed: 95th p90 p99 results uploaded to https://go/loadtest/results/789

frank: saw the results briefly  looks like mapping approach holds up under 10k concurrent connections. postmortem for the one failure attached.

leo: thanks. good progress.
